findings.source_quote: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire –Matthew 3:11-12.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the phrase 'Whose fan is in his hand' into idiomatic Dutch; replace 'Zijn wan is in Zijn hand' with 'Zijn waaier/ven (of: Zijn dorswaaier) is in Zijn hand' (choose one idiomatic rendering). Maintain the rest of the verse translation and the Scripture reference exactly as in the source.
findings.translation_quote: Zijn wan is in Zijn hand, en Hij zal Zijn dorsvloer grondig zuiveren en Zijn tarwe bijeenbrengen in de schuur; maar Hij zal de kaf met onblusbaar vuur verbranden –Mattheüs 3:11-12.

findings.location: Paragraph describing those who rejected Jesus (following Matthew 3:11-12 block)
findings.source_quote: Those who rejected Him were blown away and disappeared from the narrative.
findings.suggested_fix: 'Verwierven' is incorrect (means 'acquired'); replace 'Degenen die Hem verwierven, werden weggeblazen' with 'Degenen die Hem verwierven' -> actually should be 'Degenen die Hem verwierven' is wrong. Correct translation: 'Degenen die Hem verwerpen/verwierven' is wrong. Use: 'Degenen die Hem verwierpen, werden weggeblazen en verdwenen uit het verhaal.'
findings.translation_quote: Degenen die Hem verwierven, werden weggeblazen en verdwenen uit het verhaal.

findings.location: Paragraph about Luke's account (multiple occurrences of 'Doctor Luke' / 'Artsen-Lukas')
findings.source_quote:
Doctor Luke tells us that Jesus healed her of evil spirits and infirmities.
...Doctor Luke records an account of a man who was paralyzed.
findings.suggested_fix: 'Doctor Luke' should be rendered idiomatically in Dutch. Replace 'Artsen-Lukas' with 'Lucas, de dokter' or 'Lucas, de arts' (e.g. 'Lucas vertelt ons dat...'). Preserve the rest of the sentence and Scripture references.
findings.translation_quote:
Artsen-Lukas vertelt ons dat Jezus haar genas van boze geesten en ziekten.
...In Lukas 5 geeft Artsen-Lukas een verslag...

findings.location: Paragraph referring to Calvary (sentence retaining English 'for my sins—for your sins.')
findings.source_quote: …we behold our dying Lord—bleeding, dying for our sins—for my sins—for your sins.
findings.suggested_fix: The English words 'for my sins—for your sins' remain untranslated. Translate fully into Dutch and keep punctuation and emphasis consistent. Suggested replacement: '—bloedend, stervend voor onze zonden — voor mijn zonden — voor jouw zonden.' Ensure the entire quoted phrase appears in Dutch and preserve the punctuation and emphasis as in the source.
findings.translation_quote: —bloedend, stervend voor onze zonden—for mijn zonden—for jouw zonden.

findings.location: Luke 5 quotation (phrase rendered awkwardly in Dutch)
findings.source_quote:
When he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee –Luke 5:20.
…began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone? –Luke 5:21.
findings.suggested_fix: The Dutch rendering is largely correct but contains slightly awkward register in places. Optionally smooth 'zei Hij tegen hem' → 'zei Hij'. Keep Scripture references intact. This is stylistic; no change required if idiomatic consistency is preferred.
findings.translation_quote:
En toen Hij hun geloof zag, zei Hij tegen hem: Mens, uw zonden zijn u vergeven –Lukas 5:20.
…begonnen te redeneren en zeiden: Wie is deze die godslasteringen spreekt? Wie kan zonden vergeven dan God alleen? –Lukas 5:21.

findings.suggested_fix: Alt text translation is acceptable but consider using standard contemporary Dutch phrasing: 'Zonsopgang boven ruige bergtoppen' rather than 'ruwe bergtoppen'. This is optional and stylistic.
